abstract: Diffractive deep neural networks (D 2 NNs) enable ultrafast and energy-efficient inference through free-space propagation. However, their performance on multi-class problems can be limited by shallow network depth, coupled decision boundaries, and sensitivity to detection noise. We propose a task-decomposition optical neural network (T-ONN), a multi-channel architecture that divides a complex K-class task into cooperative low-complexity subtasks based on inter-class similarity. Each subtask is implemented by a shallow diffractive network with a dedicated detector readout, and the final label is determined by combining the subtask outputs. Numerical simulations show that a two-layer T-ONN achieves 96.2% accuracy on MNIST, approaching the 96.8% accuracy of a three-layer conventional single-channel D 2 NN. On a hybrid MNIST + Fashion-MNIST 20-class task, the three-layer T-ONN reaches 94.0% accuracy and degrades more gradually under the evaluated detector-noise models than the baseline. The 10-class implementation resolves the complete task with only three shallow channels—one coarse router and two conditional five-class classifiers—demonstrating the modular advantage of task decomposition at fixed per-channel depth. The present results are simulation-based and do not constitute a claim of reduced total optical resources.
title: Simulated task-decomposed multi-channel diffractive neural networks for scalable and robust shallow-layer optical multiclass classification
